name: La Jolla Difference Sets Repository

credit.statement: Difference-set records come from the La Jolla Difference Sets Repository, compiled and maintained by Daniel M. Gordon at the IDA Center for Communications Research-La Jolla, and published as an open dataset under CC-BY-4.0.
credit.requested_citation: The dataset ships a CITATION.cff asking that it be cited using that file's metadata: Daniel M. Gordon, "La Jolla Difference Sets Repository", dataset, version 1.0, 2024, https://doi.org/10.5281/zenodo.10775931. The CC-BY-4.0 licence also requires stating what was changed: only open parameter sets are kept here, and no difference sets are copied.

retrieval.method: Fetch the published ds.json dataset, keep entries whose upstream status is "Open", and quote the entry itself as evidence. The dmgordon.org search form is POST-only, so the JSON file is both the discovery index and the evidence. The two were cross-checked by hand: the site's open-status search returns 10037 rows, all with v below 50000, and they match the dataset's open entries in that range exactly.

redistribution.note: Records store the parameters, the abelian group's invariant factors, and the quoted status entry. No difference sets are copied from the dataset.

caveats: The dataset lists only parameter sets with v < 100000 that pass the counting, Schutzenberger and Bruck-Ryser-Chowla tests, so absence from it is not a nonexistence claim.

The maintainer states that an attempt has been made to include all known difference sets but that Paley sets are omitted for v > 1000 and some constructions are not yet included, so an "Open" row means unknown to this database rather than unknown to the literature.
The maintainer asks to be told about difference sets, nonexistence results or errors not in the database, which is an explicit statement that it may be incomplete.
The upstream search form at dmgordon.org posts its query, so it cannot be used as a stable evidence URL; every row cites the published JSON dataset instead.
The published dataset reaches further than the website search, which returns nothing above v = 50000, so rows above that were checked against the dataset alone.
This release contains a subset selected under an earlier computational-cost cap; the upstream dataset holds 102719 open cases in total.

Only existence in the specific abelian group named by the invariant factors is open; the same (v, k, lambda) may be settled in a different group, and nonabelian groups are out of scope for this dataset.
The databases are being retired: the maintainer states there will be no changes after March 1, 2026, and the data lives on at GitHub and Zenodo.
